commit_message:
The simple API applies the logging settings (AU_LOGGING_LEVEL, AU_LOGGING_ENABLED) (#26)

* The simple API applies the logging settings (AU_LOGGING_LEVEL, AU_LOGGING_ENABLED) (#22)

The default backend the simple API builds now carries a LoggingMiddleware
at config.logging_level when config.logging_enabled (default True, as
documented). Both settings were loaded and never read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review fixes: au logs nothing unless configured; a bad level names its setting (#22)

- A NullHandler on the "au" logger: a failing task no longer prints a
  traceback to stderr in an app that has not configured logging (the
  caller gets the error from get_result anyway).
- _middleware_from_config builds the middleware and re-raises a bad
  AU_LOGGING_LEVEL under the setting's name.
- The config docs say logging_level is the level task start/end is logged
  at, not a filter.
- Tests: AU_LOGGING_LEVEL changes what is logged (caplog), isolated from
  ambient AU_* variables and config files; the refusal; the NullHandler.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-review fixes: quiet only the task logger, keep au's own errors visible (#22)

The NullHandler on "au" also hid errors au catches and only logs (a result
the store could not write, a failing hook), which master printed to stderr.
The simple API's task logging now goes to its own "au.tasks" logger, and
only that one has a NullHandler. The test fixture also sets USERPROFILE,
which Path.home() reads on Windows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------
